parameters.title: Select spectral bands per indicator by univariate (F-test) selection
parameters.label: Select the spectral bands with the strongest univariate (F-test) relation to an indicator (SelectKBest). Needs a dataframe with spectra and indicators, e.g. a compiled dataset; covariates are not selected, and only used as indicators when named in indicator_array. Selected on the training samples; with separate_selections regression_modeling refits the selection on its own training samples.

parameter.hint: The root fp of the project
The dataframe to use as input, raw = original spectra, previous = the latest saved parquet file(s), or state the name of the parquet file with spectra derived from earlier step(s) to use as input.
Indicators to select bands for; empty = every numeric indicator of the dataframe except the covariates of a compiled dataset (a covariate named here is processed).
If the selection should be done sepately for each indicator, false = all indicators in one selection (single dataframe output); true= individual dataframes will be created for each indicator.
Optional JSON with {"SelectKBest": {"n_features": 20}} (path relative to the project root); none = use n_features.
Number of bands to retain, saved without asking; overrides the selector file. 0 = from univariate_selector_fp, then asked before saving.

Fraction of the samples held out as test samples (hash of the sample id, the same holdout as regression_modeling). The bands are selected from the remaining training samples only. Must equal test_size of regression_modeling, otherwise the selection is flagged as made with test samples included. 0 = use all samples.
Colour ramp for plotting spectra: a matplotlib colormap name, or default = the spectra_plot parameter set (ml_setting, "jet").
Maximum number of spectra drawn in the plot.
Save the selection plot(s) (plot/selection_plot for permutation/RFE/tree, plus the band scores under band_selection/; plot/ for univariate).
Optional user extension (1-6 letters, digits or -) added to the file suffix after a hashtag, e.g. .c-org-plsr-pms#k20, to tell apart outputs with different settings.
